text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch institutions' investments in foreign securities has grown rapidly in recent years, central bank Q2 report says.(p13)
-- Prime Minister Kok says should be possible to maintain link between private-sector wages and social security payments for years to come. (p1)
-- Small and medium-sized businesses set to account for almost half of Dutch jobs growth this year, says CPB. (p5)
-- Begemann posts H1 net profit of 14.5 million guilders and forecasts small profit for full year 1996. (p3)
-- Temp employment firm Content posts 23 pct rise in H1 net and sees substantial rise in profit in full '96.(p1)
VOLKSKRANT
-- Frits Bolkestein, leader of Liberal (VVD) coalition partner, accused by TV programme of abusing position as director of MSD pharmaceuticals firm to lobby Health Minister to favour company. (p1)

-- Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm wants to use Dutch presidency of EU next year to brain-storm improvements in how EU budget negotiated, rather than see scrapping over how much each member puts in and gets out. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
-- Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm wants Germans to hike fuel prices. (p1)
-- Changes in Aruba judiciary in attempt to halt chaos (p1)
-- Defence ministry to pay 30,000 guilders each to relatives of 34 victims of Hercules plane that crashed at Eindhoven military airport in July. (p3)
-- Docters van Leeuwen, head of state judiciary, calls for global legalisation of soft drugs. (p6)
-- Central Bank wants greater supervision of investment funds, including environmental funds. (p11)
-- Ice-cream consumption fell sharply due to poor summer - association (p11)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
-- Computer problems meant bank ABN AMRO failed to spot biggest fraud in Dutch banking history with 25 million guilders laundered and exported (p1)
-- Feyenoord chairman says too much live-TV soccer is hitting match attendances (p1)
-- Unions at Douwe Egberts agree new employment terms. (p11)
TROUW
-- Lower House shocked at claim that African women requesting asylum in the Netherlands end up in prostitution (p1)
